audit.whatIsWrong: Every row disagreed with the page's own whys. Stored chart was Quinn / Skill x5 / Quinn; the whys describe even / Quinn / Quinn / you / you / Quinn / you — which is the packet chart exactly.
audit.why: Quinn owns levels 2-3 on Vault and again at her first item; Urgot owns 4-5, level 6 and the late game. The run of Skill rows flattened a two-swing lane into nothing.
audit.corrected: All seven rows proposed as matched full/content pairs to the packet shape, ratings aligned, and phases[1].why, phases[2].why and phases[5].why rewritten because they described Urgot winning rows that now correctly read Quinn.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1].text ends 'before Tag-Team repositions her out'. There is no ability called Tag-Team in Quinn's kit.
audit.why: Her R is Behind Enemy Lines. It is on a 3s cooldown but Riot's kit flags it as a channel, which is the interaction that actually matters: Disdain (E) or Fear Beyond Death cancels it outright, so she cannot leave a lost fight by flying away.
audit.corrected: Fabricated name removed and replaced with the real, verified interaction — your R cancels Behind Enemy Lines because it is a channel.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four strings call Vault a 'knockback' — 'her E (Vault) knockback', 'Vault knockback', 'Dashes to a target, knocks back', 'Vault in, burst, and dash out'.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Quinn dashes to an enemy, dealing physical damage and slowing the target's Move Speed. Upon reaching the target, she leaps off the target, briefly interrupting it, and lands near her maximum Attack Range away.' Nothing displaces YOU. It interrupts you and repositions HER to range. That distinction changes the counterplay completely: you are not thrown out of your own Purge, you are stopped for an instant while she resets spacing — so the answer is to hold Disdain for after the Vault, not to expect to be knocked away.
audit.corrected: Vault is 12s at rank 1 to 8s: it dashes in, briefly interrupts you, and drops her back at max attack range. Blinding Assault (Q) is 11s at rank 1, 1025 range, and blinds your basic attacks. Flip her while Vault is down.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns listed Vault twice and gave no numbers.
audit.why: Vault's 12s and Blinding Assault's 11s are the two clocks the lane is played on.
audit.corrected: Both written in with what each one actually does to you.

edits.before: E or W second depending on kill pressure. A landed E-flip into W spray already wins most level-2 exchanges outright.
edits.after: Vault (E), 12s at rank 1, dashes in, interrupts you and lands her back at max range — you have no answer yet.

edits.before: Full legs rotation online — this is your lane now. Walk Quinn down with W whenever Vault (Dash/Blind) is on cooldown.
edits.after: She repeats Vault every 12s and Blinding Assault every 11s — only walk her down with Purge while both are spent.

edits.before: Black Cleaver stacks instantly with W — your shred turns even tanky answers soft. Shove and force Quinn to trade into the spike.
edits.after: Her first item revives the burst: Blinding Assault into Vault wins a straight trade if you stand still. Keep minions between you.

edits.before: Quinn's power window: her E (Vault) knockback plus Blinding Assault give her repeated all-in windows before you can trade back. Bait the Vault, then land Q (Corrosive Charge) as she dashes in and W (Purge) her down while her mobility is spent.
edits.after: Quinn's power window: Vault (E, 12s) dashes in, interrupts you, then drops her back at max range, and Blinding Assault (Q, 11s) blinds your autos. Bait the Vault, land Corrosive Charge as she dashes, then Purge her while it is down.

edits.before: Your R (Fear Beyond Death) lets you flip a fight the moment she commits. If she Vaults in for a trade, Purge her low and R to execute before Tag-Team repositions her out.
edits.after: Fear Beyond Death (R) punishes the moment she commits: if she Vaults in, Purge her low and execute. It also cancels Behind Enemy Lines, which is a channel.

edits.before: Levels 3-6 favour Quinn. Her Vault knockback and Blinding Assault give her repeated all-in windows, and your slow legs cannot punish her if you misposition; keep minions between you and only trade when her E is down.
edits.after: Levels 2-3 and again at her first item favour Quinn. Vault (12s) interrupts you and lands her back at range, and Blinding Assault (11s) blinds your basic attacks. Trade only while Vault is down, and keep minions between you.

edits.before: Vault in, burst, and dash out before you leg it back
edits.after: Vault in, interrupt you, land back at max range

edits.before: - Quinn Vault (Dash/Blind): matchup-defining — Her self-peel. Flip her with your E. Track it before every engage. - Quinn Vault: Dashes to a target, knocks back, and blinds their next attacks. Dodge or sidestep it.
edits.after: - Vault (E), 12s at rank 1 to 8s: dashes in, interrupts you, then lands her at max range — flip her while it is down. - Blinding Assault (Q), 11s: blinds your basic attacks, so bait it on the wave.

edits.before: Her self-peel. Flip her with your E. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Her self-peel and escape, 12s at rank 1. Flip her once it is spent.

notes: MIRROR CONFLICT, flagged not resolved: quinn__urgot reports rows 0-5 all Quinn, row 6 Urgot. The packet chart and this page's own whys agree with each other and disagree with that on rows 0, 3 and 4 — whys[3] and whys[4] explicitly say those levels are Urgot's, and whys[0] says level 1 is even. I aligned to the two agreeing sources. Also carried over from the mirror and left unasserted: whether Blinding Assault's blind suppresses Echoing Flames leg blasts is not answerable from Riot's text, so I wrote only that it blinds basic attacks and made no claim about the passive. Note the full layer already described Vault correctly as a dash while the content layer called it a knockback four times — the two layers were contradicting each other.
